verdict.rationale: GitHub Projects' own custom fields let items carry metadata, and the docs explicitly show a single-select priority field (Low/Medium/High) and project-level status updates such as "On track" or "At risk". An owning-team attribute is only implied: custom fields could hold it, but the documented grouping is by individual assignee, not team. Missing for 10: an explicitly documented owning-team field or team-level grouping, explicit per-initiative status-field documentation beyond project-level status updates, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can track initiatives with status, priority, and an owning team

citations.quote: You can use custom fields to add metadata to your issues, pull requests, and draft issues and build a richer view of item attributes.
A single select field to track whether a task is Low, Medium, or High priority.
You can set a status, such as "On track" or "At risk", to allow people to quickly determine the current state of the project.
group your project by assignee, and make changes to issue assignment by dragging issues into the different groups.
